canonicalExplanation.summary: **Natural-language processing** (NLP) covers many tasks: splitting text into **tokens**, turning it into **representations**, **classifying** it (spam, topic), **extracting** facts (names, dates), **retrieving** relevant documents, **translating** and **generating**. Each needs its own evaluation, matched to the **task**, the **languages and dialects** users actually write in, and the **cost of errors**. A model tested on standard English may fail on regional dialects, code-switching (mixing languages), slang or typos. Text-overlap scores like BLEU compare words, not meaning. Compare with a simple **keyword baseline**, report results **per language or dialect**, and route **uncertain, high-cost** cases to a person.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A learner's support classifier scores 92% on an English benchmark and is launched in India. Tickets in Hinglish (Hindi mixed with English) are routed wrongly half the time, and urgent ones sit in the wrong queue for days. A support classifier reports per-language and dialect confusion metrics against a keyword baseline and sends uncertain high-cost cases to review. In this lesson you'll frame and evaluate a small NLP task while identifying language and dialect coverage gaps.

sections.heading: The model: task-matched, slice-aware NLP evaluation
sections.body:
```python
URGENT = {"down", "outage", "not working", "band hai"}   # includes one Hindi phrase.

def keyword_baseline(text):
    return "urgent" if any(k in text.lower() for k in URGENT) else "normal"

tickets = [  # (text, language variety, true label)
    ("Site is down", "en", "urgent"), ("Please update my email", "en", "normal"),
    ("App band hai since morning", "hinglish", "urgent"),
    ("payment fail ho gaya", "hinglish", "urgent"), ("bill chahiye", "hinglish", "normal"),
]

for lang in ("en", "hinglish"):
    rows = [t for t in tickets if t[1] == lang]
    correct = sum(keyword_baseline(t[0]) == t[2] for t in rows)
    print(lang, f"{correct}/{len(rows)} correct")
# Report per slice; send uncertain urgent-looking tickets to review.
```

| Task | Evaluate with |
|---|---|
| classification. | per-slice confusion counts. |
| extraction. | field-level precision and recall. |
| generation. | task success and factual checks, not only overlap. |

```reveal
{"prompt": "Why is a keyword baseline useful?", "answer": "It's cheap and transparent. If a model can't beat it on each language slice, the model's complexity isn't earning its keep there."}
```

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: One English benchmark or text-overlap metric establishes that an NLP system understands language and works for all dialects.
misconceptions.correction: Performance must be measured per language, dialect and task, with metrics matched to what users need.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The Hinglish misroute", what was missing from evaluation?

analogy.example: An NLP system is like **a call-centre agent trained with one accent**. They do well with callers who sound like the training tapes, but struggle with other accents and mixed languages. You'd test them **with every kind of caller you actually get**, and let them **transfer hard calls** to a colleague.
usefulFor: remembering test every kind of caller
limitations: A phrasebook is the keyword baseline.
Word-overlap scores are like grading by matching words, not meaning.
